card.name: Co-infection wording after HIV/HCV
card.fires_on: The start of "co-infected" or "coinfection" right after a pair of viruses such as HIV-1/HCV or HBV/HIV-1. It fires on "co", "-in", "-inf" or "Coin".

modes.label: Co before hyphen
modes.description: The "co" that begins "co-infected" right after HIV-1/HCV.
modes.example: lamivudine in HIV-1/HCV<< co>>-infected patients [see Clinical Pharmacology

modes.label: Inside co-infected
modes.description: The "-inf" or "-in" piece in the middle of "co-infected" or "co-infection".
modes.example: Hepatic decompensation, some fatal, has occurred in HIV-1/HCV co<<-inf>>ected patients receiving combination antiretrov

modes.label: Coinfection spelled solid
modes.description: "Coin" starting the unhyphenated word "coinfection" after HBV/HIV-1.
modes.example: Patients with HBV/HIV-1<< Coin>>fection Who Discontinue Nucleos(t

card.writes: It favors words meaning two things at once, like "simultaneously" and "compound", which suits co-occurring conditions.
card.plain: It lights up on the start of "co-infected" when a label names patients with two viruses at once.
